title: Flat pullback commutes with ideal powers
statement:
Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal. If
$g\colon Y\to X$ is flat, then the image of $g^*(\mathcal I^n)$ in
$\mathcal O_Y$ is $(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y)^n$ for every $n$.

proof.text: Fix $n\in\mathbf N$. By [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], $\mathcal I^0=\mathcal O_X$ and the product of two quasi-coherent ideal sheaves is quasi-coherent. Induction using $\mathcal I^{m+1}=\mathcal I^m\mathcal I$ therefore shows that every $\mathcal I^m$ is quasi-coherent. For each $m$, take the closed subscheme $i_m:Z_m=V(\mathcal I^m)\hookrightarrow X$ cut out by $\mathcal I^m$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme]. Its ideal is exactly $\mathcal I^m$. Let $q_m:Z_m\times_XY\to Y$ be the projection, and write $\mathcal Q_m=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to(q_m)_*\mathcal O_{Z_m\times_XY})$.

source.place: Tag 01IN, lemma-closed-subspace-scheme; powers as in def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers

proof.text: By [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image], $q_m$ is a closed immersion and $\mathcal Q_m=\operatorname{Im}(g^*(\mathcal I^m)\to\mathcal O_Y)$, for the composite induced by $\mathcal I^m\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$ and the structural map $g^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$. By [def-nagata-extended-ideal], $\mathcal Q_m=(\mathcal I^m)\mathcal O_Y$; in particular put $\mathcal J=\mathcal Q_1=\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y$. The closed-immersion ideal description [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] shows that each $\mathcal Q_m$, hence $\mathcal J$, is quasi-coherent. Thus the powers of $\mathcal J$ used below are defined. The two orders of the fibre product have the same projection to $Y$ under its canonical symmetry.

The affine-open basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] gives an affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $g(y)$ and an affine open $V\subseteq g^{-1}(U)$ containing $y$, for every $y\in Y$. Consequently all such pairs $(U,V)$ cover $Y$. Fix any such pair and set $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $B=\mathcal O_Y(V)$, $I=\mathcal I(U)$, and $\varphi=g^\sharp_{U,V}:A\to B$. The affine extension formula [lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension], applied to $i_m$ and $g$, gives $\mathcal Q_m(V)=\langle\varphi(\mathcal I^m(U))\rangle_B$. By [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], $\mathcal I^m(U)=I^m$. In particular $\mathcal J(V)=\langle\varphi(I)\rangle_B=IB$. This computes the sections of the ideal subsheaf $\mathcal Q_m$ after the sheaf-image identification in step 2; it does not assume that taking sections commutes with images of module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens; Tag 01JU, lemma-fibre-product-immersion (1), affine form; Tag 01IN, lemma-closed-subspace-scheme

proof.text: Apply the general ring-map clause of [lemma-nagata-localization-ideal-pow] to $\varphi:A\to B$ and $I$. It gives $(I^n)B=(IB)^n$, with no localization or injectivity hypothesis on $\varphi$. Combining this with step 3 and the affine power formula of [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers] for $\mathcal J$ yields $\mathcal Q_n(V)=(I^n)B=(IB)^n=\mathcal J(V)^n=(\mathcal J^n)(V)$ as ideals inside $B$. For $n=0$ both sides are $B$, since $I^0=A$ and $\varphi(1)=1$. This calculation holds for every adapted affine pair $(U,V)$, not only one chosen cover.

We now check equality on any open $T\subseteq Y$ directly. For each $y\in T$ choose $U$ and then an affine $V$ containing $y$ and contained in $T\cap g^{-1}(U)$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. These $V$ cover $T$ and step 4 gives $\mathcal Q_n(V)=\mathcal J^n(V)$ inside $\mathcal O_Y(V)$. A section of $\mathcal Q_n(T)$ therefore restricts to sections of $\mathcal J^n$ on this cover; they agree on overlaps because both sheaves inject into $\mathcal O_Y$. The sheaf axiom glues them to a section of $\mathcal J^n(T)$ whose image is the original section, by uniqueness of gluing in $\mathcal O_Y$. Interchanging the two sheaves proves the reverse inclusion. Hence $\mathcal Q_n=\mathcal J^n$ as ideal subsheaves, and step 2 identifies this with the required image equality.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal. If
$g\colon Y\to X$ is flat, then the image of $g^*(\mathcal I^n)$ in
$\mathcal O_Y$ is $(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Y)^n$ for every $n$.

proof.text:
Work on an affine chart, with a flat ring map $A\to B$ and ideal $I\subseteq A$. Tensoring $0\to I^n\to A$ with $B$ gives an injection
$I^n\otimes_AB\to B$. Its image is generated by the elements $xb$ with
$x\in I^n$ and $b\in B$, which is exactly $(IB)^n$: expand products of
generators for one inclusion and write elements of $I^n$ as finite sums of
products for the other. These equalities commute with localization, so
they glue to the asserted equality of ideal sheaves.
